newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha prices easier in subdued trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha prices easier in subdued trade.

text.p: Naphtha prices fell on Friday mirroring bearish overnight crudes, traders said. Trading remained listless due to a lack of firm buyers, they added.
"It's so much easier to find sellers than buyers," one trader said. "Buyers are worried whether naphtha will fall even further."
Offers for second-half March open-spec naphtha were heard at $238.00, while bids were notionally assessed at $237.00. It was sold at $239.00 to a western trader on Thursday.
First-half April was assessed at around $235.00/236.00, compared with late Thursday's $239.00/240.00.
The second-half March/second-half April spread was talked at plus $3.50/5.00 after it was traded at $4.00 on Thursday.
Naphtha spreads have been shrinking this week on the back of recovered availability for near-term cargoes.
Naphtha's supply and demand balance became relaxed for prompt cargoes due to slower-than-expected end-user demand, traders said.
Weaker middle distillate prices in Singapore are expected to prompt some oil firms in Japan to start seeking second-half February jet cargoes, traders said.
